channel.title: Variator QA
channel.description: Most recent changes with links to updates.

item.title: Version 0.4.1.3 (2536) QA
item.description:
What's New in Variator 0.4.1.3 (Build 2536)

Variator 0.4.1.3 candidate: hook and Suggest never write invented text and show the reason with Switch engine; batch keeps each video's own hook; the developer switch works in every build; erase failures report what stayed readable.

Your text stays.

When the text engine fails, Replace, Roll, Suggest and batch keep your text and show the reason with Switch engine; nothing invented is written.

Suggest shows what happens.

Suggest on a selected text shows progress and, if it fails, the same reason row as Hook; an old answer never overwrites newer text.

Developer switch works.

The hidden developer gesture works in every build again.

Erase failures explain themselves.

When erased text stays readable, the log names the frames, boxes and coverage.

item.title: Version 0.4.1.3 (2525) QA
item.description:
What's New in Variator 0.4.1.3 (Build 2525)

Variator 0.4.1.3 candidate: canvas clicks, handles and rotated layers behave as drawn; subtitles match the export at cue edges, avoid burned text and group the same words; padded 16:9 text matches the export.

Click what you see.

A fresh click selects the top layer you see; a repeat click at the same point goes to the layer below. Choosing a layer in the list starts fresh. Rotated layers are clicked by their shape. Hidden tracked layers show no handles.

Subtitles match the video.

The paused preview shows a subtitle only while it is on screen in the export, ends it at the same frame, keeps a kept subtitle when an overlapping one is removed, and groups the same words as the export after a trim.

Subtitles avoid burned text.

Speech subtitles are placed clear of every burned caption and move when text is found late.

16:9 text stays where you put it.

On a 16:9 video in a 9:16 frame, text is drawn in the preview where the export draws it.

Long variable-frame-rate videos map fully.

Every frame of a long variable-frame-rate video is read, not only the first part.

item.title: Version 0.4.1.3 (2506) QA
item.description:
What's New in Variator 0.4.1.3 (Build 2506)

Variator 0.4.1.3 candidate: canvas clicks select what you see, scale arrows scale, late burned captions are found, Erase Region ignores texture noise, the hook Font row is back with TikTok Sans as default, plus the 2487 fixes.

Clicks select what you see.

A click on the preview selects the element shown at that moment; a hidden element no longer takes the click.

Scale arrows scale.

Pressing the corner arrows of a selected element scales it; rotation starts only from the round handle.

Late captions are found.

Burned captions anywhere in the video become editable layers, not only the first seconds.

Erase ignores texture noise.

Two or three letters read from clothing or background no longer fail an Erase Region export.

TikTok Sans by default; Font row in the Hook card.

Hook, banner and subtitles start in TikTok Sans; the Hook card Font row edits the same font as Fine-tune Hook.

Analyze finishes reliably.

On a busy Mac, Analyze sometimes failed with 'completed analysis event did not include artifactPath' after it had finished. The app now reads the whole result before it continues.

Text stays inside the frame.

A text block placed near an edge is moved inward so no letter is cut off, in the preview and in the export.

Videos with an odd width or height render.

A video such as 719x1280 now renders at the nearest even size instead of failing.

No microphone prompt.

Exporting no longer makes macOS ask for microphone access.

Phone videos with an uneven frame rate render on the Engine.

Clips that move between 24 and 30 frames per second keep the same picture as the preview.

Subtitles in the export match the preview.

Speech subtitles break into the same phrases in the preview and in the exported video.

Karaoke highlights the spoken word in every export.

The TikTok Karaoke style lights the current word also when the export uses the fallback renderer.

Studio Hard works on videos without a face.

A caption-only video renders without the spotlight instead of stopping with an error.

Local models keep to their own folder.

Model downloads no longer read or write your personal Hugging Face cache or token.

item.title: Version 0.4.1.2 (2457) QA
item.description:
What's New in Variator 0.4.1.2 (Build 2457)

Variator 0.4.1.2 candidate: speech subtitles and your own fonts reach the export, HDR stays HDR, Thai hooks read correctly, 29.97, 60 fps and variable-frame-rate phone videos render on the Engine, and a crash during diagnostics upload is fixed.

Speech subtitles are in the export.

In Studio and Localization the subtitles you see in the preview are now burned into the exported video.

Your own fonts reach the export.

A font you dropped in or downloaded is used in the exported video, not only in the preview.

HDR stays HDR.

An HDR iPhone clip keeps its HDR colour in the preview and in the export.

Thai hook text is read in Thai.

A hook written in one non-Latin script is read in its own language; a mixed or unreadable hook shows a reason.

The Liliya recipe keeps the voice pitch.

The Standard UGC recipe no longer raises the voice pitch.

The banner names only your delivered variations.

A freshly imported video no longer shows a 'Derived Variation' banner from old test runs; the banner names only variations of the open video that you delivered.

Every export gets its own name.

Exports are named from their own result instead of a fixed placeholder, so repeated exports to one folder no longer collide as -2, -3, -4.

No developer controls in the release build.

A packaged build hides the DEV badge, Lab, Arcade and Dock Animation and is stamped as a candidate.

29.97 and 60 fps videos render like the preview.

Videos at 29.97, 23.976, 59.94 and 60 frames per second now go through the same renderer as the preview, so the export matches what you see.

Phone videos with an uneven frame rate keep their full length.

A video whose frame rate changes while recording no longer loses its last half second, and its picture stays in step with the sound.

No more quits after a diagnostics upload.

The app no longer closes during work shortly after it sends its diagnostics.

Your recipe choice stays when you apply a recipe.

Apply Recipe keeps the goal you picked instead of switching it back.
